summary: Rewired `tldr deps` rust import-to-module resolution so workspace cross-crate `use other_crate::foo` and intra-crate `use crate::foo::bar` both resolve correctly, and `mod foo;` declarations look for SIBLING files instead of falling through to a global bare-name match.

root_cause.headline: Global bare-name index funnelled all `mod tests;` (and similar) into whichever rust file happened to be named `tests.rs` first, with no per-crate context for workspace-style projects.
details: `index_rust_module` unconditionally inserted every rust file under its basename — `tests`, `walk`, `lib`, `mod` — into a single `HashMap<String, PathBuf>` namespace.

ripgrep's 9-crate workspace has dozens of files containing `mod tests;` at the bottom (unit test modules). Each of those bare-name lookups hit the FIRST `tests.rs` indexed, which happened to be the top-level integration test file `tests/tests.rs`. Result: 36 spurious incoming edges to `tests/tests.rs`.
Cross-crate `use ignore::WalkState` from `crates/core/main.rs` fell through entirely — nothing in the index spelled `ignore`.

Intra-crate `use crate::flags` worked by accident on `crates/core/main.rs` because `crates/core/flags/mod.rs` happened to be the first file indexed under `crate::flags`; other crates with same-named submodules would lose the race.

approach: Per-file crate discovery: `find_rust_crate_root` walks up from each rust file to the nearest ancestor `Cargo.toml`, reads `[package].name` / `[lib].name` via a hand-rolled mini-parser (`read_cargo_package_name`), and reports the crate root + crate name.
`build_module_index` does a single up-front pre-pass for rust to map each file to its owning crate root (cached so a workspace with N files in the same crate only parses one Cargo.toml).

Rewritten `index_rust_module(index, file_path, relative, crate_info)`: registers each file under `<crate_name>::<src_rel>` for cross-crate lookup; registers the bare crate name for lib.rs/main.rs (crate root module); records sibling-file metadata under a reserved `\0rust_meta::sibling::<dir>::<name>` key; stashes per-file crate root + src-relative module path under reserved `\0rust_meta::file::...` / `\0rust_meta::src_rel::...` keys (NUL byte ensures collision-free coexistence with real rust paths in the shared map). The unconditional global bare-name insertion is REMOVED.

Rewritten `resolve_rust_import(module, current_file, index)`: stdlib filter -> bare-name sibling resolution -> `crate::`/`self::`/`super::` rewritten to absolute `<crate_name>::...` via stashed metadata -> direct cross-crate lookup with progressive `::`-prefix shrink. Synthetic `\0rust_meta::` keys are explicitly filtered from the shrink fallback path.
preserved: Legacy `crate::<path-as-mod-form>` registration kept as fallback for non-crate-detected projects (entry().or_insert_with so crate-aware entries win on collision).
Kotlin deps wiring (W-H, 2addf07) unchanged and re-verified by the new test.

post_fix.explanation: Total internal deps dropped 172->140 because 32 spurious bare-name matches were eliminated. The 140 remaining edges have a balanced distribution (max single-target = 13, was 36) and correctly include workspace cross-crate edges that were previously invisible.

cases.name: rust_deps_has_non_zero_modules
cases.verifies: deps returns >0 files & >0 edges on ripgrep; AND no single target receives >5 incoming edges from spurious bare-name `mod tests;` matches (pre-fix: 36, post-fix: absent from top 10).

cases.name: rust_deps_resolves_intra_crate_use
cases.verifies: concrete edge crates/core/main.rs -> crates/core/flags/mod.rs (intra-crate `use crate::flags`), plus >=5 intra-crate edges across the workspace as a whole.

cases.name: kotlin_deps_still_wires
cases.verifies: non-regression — kotlin-datetime still has >=100 internal edges (W-H baseline: 317).

scope_notes.in_scope: Workspace-aware crate-root discovery via Cargo.toml; sibling-file resolution for `mod foo;`; `crate::`/`self::`/`super::` rewriting; cross-crate `use other_crate::foo`; stdlib filter.
scope_notes.out_of_scope: Macro-imported re-exports (`pub use other_crate::foo as bar`), feature-gated `#[cfg(...)]` modules, build.rs-generated module paths. The fix uses purely lexical resolution off the file tree + Cargo.toml — no `cargo metadata` invocation or macro expansion.
